outline: Diagnosis and differentiation from ischemic and inflammatory mimics
primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy is a transient nonischemic left ventricular systolic dysfunction that often follows intense emotional or physical stress and can mimic acute coronary syndrome. Characteristic ventricular dysfunction extends beyond a single epicardial coronary distribution, often with apical and midventricular akinesis and basal hyperkinesis, while coronary angiography lacks an obstructive culprit lesion or acute plaque rupture.
vignette: A 69-year-old woman develops sudden substernal chest pressure shortly after receiving news of the unexpected death of her spouse. An ECG shows ST-segment elevation in the anterior precordial leads, and serum troponin is mildly elevated. Urgent coronary angiography shows no obstructive coronary artery disease or evidence of acute plaque rupture. Left ventriculography shows akinesis of the apical and midventricular segments with hyperdynamic contraction of the base; the wall-motion abnormality extends beyond the territory of a single epicardial coronary artery. Cardiac MRI shows myocardial edema without a corresponding pattern of late gadolinium enhancement.
lead: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
distractors: Acute anterior myocardial infarction due to left anterior descending artery occlusion
distractor_notes: An anterior myocardial infarction caused by LAD occlusion produces ischemic injury in the LAD distribution and ordinarily has an obstructive or thrombotic culprit mechanism. The absence of an obstructive culprit lesion together with wall-motion abnormalities extending beyond one vascular territory argues against this diagnosis.

Myocarditis can cause chest pain, troponin elevation, ECG abnormalities, and nonischemic ventricular dysfunction, but cardiac MRI in acute myocarditis commonly demonstrates inflammatory tissue abnormalities such as nonischemic late gadolinium enhancement. The abrupt stress trigger and characteristic apical/midventricular ballooning pattern without a corresponding LGE pattern more strongly support takotsubo cardiomyopathy.

Coronary vasospasm can produce rest angina and transient ischemic ST-segment changes without fixed obstructive coronary disease. However, its diagnosis relies on evidence of transient coronary spasm or characteristic nitrate-responsive episodes; it does not best explain the characteristic stress-associated ventricular ballooning extending beyond a single coronary territory.

Acute pericarditis classically produces pleuritic or positional chest pain with diffuse concave ST elevation and/or PR depression and may show pericardial inflammation or effusion. Those findings do not explain the characteristic apical and midventricular systolic dysfunction with basal hyperkinesis in this vignette.
key_expl: This presentation is most consistent with takotsubo cardiomyopathy. The syndrome often mimics an acute myocardial infarction with chest pain, ECG abnormalities, and a modest biomarker rise, but the ventricular dysfunction is transient and extends beyond a single epicardial coronary distribution, while coronary angiography shows no obstructive culprit lesion or acute plaque rupture. A major emotional stressor and apical/midventricular akinesis with basal hyperkinesis are characteristic clues. Cardiac MRI can show myocardial edema without the corresponding late gadolinium enhancement pattern expected from myocardial infarction or typical inflammatory myocarditis.
objective: Recognize takotsubo cardiomyopathy in a patient with an acute coronary-syndrome-like presentation after major stress when ventricular wall-motion abnormalities extend beyond a single coronary territory and angiography shows no obstructive culprit lesion.
clues: older woman after major emotional stress
acute chest pain with anterior ST elevation
apical and midventricular akinesis with basal hyperkinesis
wall-motion abnormality beyond one epicardial coronary territory
myocardial edema without corresponding late gadolinium enhancement pattern
